 Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

JUSTICE P.S. RANA (R) PRESIDENT:

O R D E R :
-
1. Present appeal is filed under
section 15
of

Consumer Protection Act 1986 against order dated

21.07.2017 passed by Learned District Forum in consumer

complaint No.85/2016 title Smt. Neelam Versus M/s. Nikhil

Communication & Ors.
Brief facts of consumer complaint:
2. Smt. Neelam filed consumer complaint under
section 12
of Consumer Protection Act 1986 pleaded therein

that complainant purchased a mobile Xperia Z-1 in

consideration amount of Rs.26190/-(Twenty six thousand one

hundred ninety). It is pleaded that mobile started giving

hanging problem within the warranty period. It is further

pleaded that mobile was handed over by complainant to

opposite party No.1 on dated 15.02.2016 who assured that

problem would be resolved. It is pleaded that on dated
22.02.2016 opposite party No.1 informed that matter was

reported to opposite party No.3 and they would issue a new

mobile to the complainant. Thereafter on 08.03.2016

complainant contacted opposite party No.1 at his shop and

opposite party No.1 refused to issue new mobile and told the

complainant that company had refused to supply new mobile

to complainant. It is further pleaded that opposite parties
2
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

have committed deficiency in service and indulged in unfair

trade practices. It is pleaded that on dated 09.03.2016

complainant also issued legal notice to opposite parties.

Complainant sought relief to the effect that opposite parties

be directed to deliver new phone or opposite parties be

directed to pay the complete costs to the tune of Rs.26190/-

(Twenty six thousand one hundred ninety) alongwith costs of

litigation to the tune of Rs.10000/-(Ten thousand) jointly and

severally alongwith interest @ 12% per annum.
3. Opposite parties did not appear before learned

District Forum despite service and learned District Forum on

dated 30.08.2016 proceeded ex-parte against opposite parties.

Thereafter opposite parties filed revision petition No.53/2016

before State Commission and revision petition was allowed

and ex-parte proceeding against opposite parties were set

aside subject to costs and parties were directed to appear

before learned District Forum on dated 19.04.2017 by State

Commission. On dated 19.04.2017 opposite parties did not

appear before learned District Forum and learned District

Forum again proceeded ex-parte against opposite parties.
4. Learned District Forum allowed the complaint and

ordered opposite parties No.1,3 & 4 to pay sum of Rs.26190/-

(Twenty six thousand one hundred ninety) to complainant

within thirty days failing which opposite parties would pay
3
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of complaint

i.e. 19.05.2010 till the amount is paid or realized. In addition

learned District Forum ordered that on receiving the amount

complainant would return Mobile to opposite party No.1

against proper receipt and identification. Learned District

Forum further ordered that opposite parties No.1,3 & 4 would

pay punitive compensation to complainant to the tune of

Rs.5000/-(Five thousand). Learned District Forum further

ordered that opposite parties No.1,3 & 4 would also pay

litigation costs to the tune of Rs.5000/-(Five thousand) to

complainant. Feeling aggrieved against order passed by

Learned District Forum opposite parties filed present appeal

before State Commission.
5. We have heard learned advocates appearing on

behalf of parties and we have also perused entire record

carefully.
6. Following points arise for determination in present

appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by appellants is liable to be
 accepted as mentioned in memorandum of
 grounds of appeal?
2. Final order.
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
7. Complainant filed affidavit annexure-C1 in

evidence. There is recital in affidavit that deponent purchase
4
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

mobile phone in consideration amount of Rs.26190/-(Twenty

six thousand one hundred ninety) from opposite party No.1.
There is recital in affidavit that during the warranty period

mobile started hanging problem. There is further recital in

affidavit that mobile was handed over to opposite party No.1

at shop. There is recital in affidavit that on 08.03.2016

opposite party No.1 refused to issue new mobile to

complainant and told the complainant that company has

refused to issue new mobile. There is further recital in

affidavit that legal notice was also issued by complainant to

opposite parties. Complainant also filed annexures C2 to C4.
8. Opposite parties did not file any version before

learned District Forum and opposite parties also did not

adduce any evidence. Evidence by way of affidavit adduced

by complainant and evidence by way of annexures adduced

by complainant before learned District Forum remained

unrebutted on record.
9. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that retail invoice bill annexure-C2 was

issued to complainant on 05.03.2015 and only warranty of

mobile was given and guarantee of mobile was not given and

on this ground appeal be allowed is decided accordingly.

State Commission has carefully perused retail invoice bill

annexure-C2 dated 05.03.2015 placed on record. It is proved
5
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

on record that Xperia Z-1 mobile phone was sold on behalf of

M/s. Nikhil Communication by opposite party No.1 in

consideration amount of Rs.26190/-(Twenty six thousand one

hundred ninety) plus vat to the tune of Rs.1310/-(One

thousand three hundred ten) total Rs.27500/-(Twenty seven

thousand five hundred). State Commission has carefully

perused the terms and conditions mentioned in retail invoice

bill annexure-C2 which are quoted in toto :-
1) Received the above goods in good condition.
2) Goods once sold will not be taken back or exchange.
3) Invoiced item carry the manufacture's warranty only.
M/s. Nikhil Communication will assist in getting the warranty

and will not be liable to any laps on the manufacture's part.
4) All disputes are subject to jurisdiction of Ghumarwin

court only.
10. In the invoice bill annexure-C2 there are

signatures of complainant and opposite party No.1 on behalf

of M/s. Nikhil Communication in English language. State

Commission is of the opinion that terms and conditions

mentioned in invoice bill annexure-C2 are binding upon both

the parties and no one could be allowed to alter the terms and

conditions mentioned in the retail invoice/cash memo

annexure-C2. Complainant is a literate person and has

signed retail invoice/cash memo in sound state of mind. See
6
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

2017(3) CPR 52 NC Haj Committee of India Versus Mohd.

Rera
IPC
and others.
11. There is positive recital in retail invoice/cash

memo that complainant has received mobile phone in good

condition and there is also condition in invoice bill/cash

memo that goods once sold would not be taken back or

exchange. There is also positive recital in invoice bill/cash

memo that invoiced item would carry manufacture's warranty

only. In appeal appellants have admitted that warranty

period was not expired and same was to be expired after 16

days when complainant filed complaint before opposite party

No.1 relating to hanging of mobile phone. It is proved on

record that complaint was filed before opposite parties within

the warranty period. State Commission is of the opinion that

during warranty period opposite parties were under legal

obligation to replace the defective parts free of any charges.
12. It is well settled law that warranty and guarantee

are two different concepts under law. It is well settled law

that in guarantee the entire replacement of good is

permissible and it is also well settled law that in warranty

replacement of only defective parts is permissible. State

Commission is of the opinion that opposite parties were under

legal obligations to replace the defective parts of mobile phone

during the warranty period free of charges. State Commission
7
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

is of the opinion that as per terms and conditions of invoice

bill/cash memo opposite parties were not under legal

obligation to refund the entire amount of good to complainant

and were not under legal obligation to exchange new mobile

phone. See 2000(1) CPJ 3 Punjab Eko Electronics Versus Sh.

Kuldip Sharma & others.
13. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of opposite parties that opposite parties are not liable

to pay punitive compensation to the tune of Rs.5000/-(Five

thousand) to complainant is decided accordingly. State

Commission is of the opinion that consumer has to approach

learned District Forum and has to engage advocate and it is

proved on record that opposite parties did not replace

defective parts of mobile during warranty period free of

charges. Opposite parties did not adduce any rebuttal

evidence and evidence adduced by complainant remained

unrebutted on record. In view of the above stated facts it is

not expedient in the ends of justice and on the principle of

natural justice to interfere in the order of punitive

compensation awarded by learned District Forum to

complainant.
14. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that learned District Forum has illegally

granted litigation costs to the tune of Rs.5000/-(Five

thousand) and on this ground appeal be allowed is decided
8
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

accordingly. State Commission is of the opinion that learned

District Forum has granted reasonable costs to complainant

because complainant has to approach learned District Forum

when opposite parties did not replace the defective parts of

mobile phone free of charges despite legal notice issued by

complainant to the opposite parties during warranty period.
15. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of complainant that order passed by learned District

Forum is in accordance with law and in accordance with

proved facts is decided accordingly. State Commission is of

the opinion that order of learned District Forum warrants

partly interference relating to payment of Rs.26190/-(Twenty

six thousand one hundred ninety) to complainant alongwith

interest @ 9% per annum from date of filing the complaint

because guarantee was not given by opposite parties to

complainant as per terms and conditions of invoice bill/cash

memo and only warranty was given to complainant as per

terms and conditions of invoice bill/cash memo annexure-C2

placed on record. In view of above stated facts point No.1 is

decided accordingly.
Point No.2: Final Order
16. In view of findings upon point No.1 above appeal is

partly allowed. Order of learned District Forum that opposite

parties No.1, 3 & 4 would pay a sum of Rs.26190/-(Twenty

six thousand one hundred ninety) to complainant alongwith
9
Sony India Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. Versus Neelam Thakur
 (F.A. No.266/2017)

interest @ 9% per annum from the date of complaint till

realization is set aside. It is ordered that opposite parties

No.3 & 4 would jointly and severally replace the defective

parts of mobile phone without claiming repair charges from

complainant within one month from the date of receipt of

certified copy of order of State Commission and opposite party

No.1 will assist in executing the warranty. Order of learned

District Forum relating to punitive compensation of Rs.5000/-

(Five thousand) is affirmed. Order of learned District Forum

relating to payment of litigation costs to the tune of Rs.5000/-

(Five thousand) is also affirmed. Order of learned District

Forum is modified to this extent only. Retail invoice/cash

memo annexure-C2 will form part and parcel of order. Parties

are left to bear their own litigation costs before State

Commission. File of learned District Forum alongwith certified

copy of order be sent back forthwith and file of State

Commission be consigned to record room after due

completion forthwith. Certified copy of order be transmitted to

parties forthwith free of costs strictly as per rules. Appeal is

disposed of. Pending application(s) if any also disposed of.
Justice P.S. Rana (R)
 President

 Vijay Pal Khachi
 Member
